bull.b: TTM operating cash flow comfortably exceeds net income and free cash flow has grown versus the prior period. This durable cash conversion supports ongoing unit openings, HEEP rollout, and large buybacks while funding capex and cushioning against cyclical pressure over the next several quarters.

Digital now constitutes a large, growing share of sales, improving order accuracy, on-time fulfillment and incremental attach rates. A durable digital mix expands reach, reduces some in-restaurant labor intensity, strengthens data-driven marketing and supports higher average checks and repeat purchasing over time.

Aggressive unit expansion (many Chipotlanes) plus HEEP equipment boosting peak throughput create structural capacity for steady comp and unit growth. New-unit productivity (~80%) and year‑2 cash-on-cash (~60%) imply durable returns from expansion and structurally higher peak-period sales per restaurant.

bear.b: A ~220bp decline in restaurant-level margins reflects persistent cost pressure (food, freight, labor). If input and wage inflation remain elevated, margin recovery will require sustained price realization or further operational gains, restraining long-term profitability and free cash flow expansion.

Higher debt-to-equity reduces financial flexibility to absorb adverse shocks or pursue opportunistic investment. Despite improvement, elevated leverage increases interest and refinancing sensitivity and constrains capital allocation choices (growth vs. buybacks) over the medium term.

Low in-store rewards capture limits ability to convert dine-in customers into tracked, higher-LTV members. This structural gap weakens personalization, targeted promotions and retention opportunities and may cap long-term comp gains unless in-restaurant enrollment and frictionless earning are widely adopted.
